actions.action: Check the outer decorative pot for standing water
Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
Trim any dead roots if found
Check stem base for softness or darkening
Repot in gritty cactus/succulent mix if roots look bad or soil is compacted
Water thoroughly until it drains and empty the saucer
Check soil is dry a couple of inches down before watering again
Bottom water for 15-20 minutes if soil seems hydrophobic
Move plant to bright light, such as a south or east window
Cut leggy stem back to a leaf node once healthy
Root the stem cutting in soil
Post a root photo if roots are mushy or smell bad

reason: The answer recognizes underwatering and hydrophobic soil but makes drought root damage the main cause; the bottom-soak fix appears only as a secondary option after root checks and repotting, which is not harmful.
